question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR's Teams multi-account public contract: `channels.msteams.accounts`/`defaultAccount`, legacy root config as the implicit default account, explicit named-account identity and webhook-port requirements, and account-scoped auth/session state?
rationale: The patch appears coherent and tested, but it sets a durable plugin configuration and state/auth compatibility contract that automation should not finalize without owner intent.

options.title: Accept the PR contract
options.body: Land the current contract with the existing exact-head checks and live Teams proof as the first supported Teams multi-account shape.

options.title: Revise before merge
options.body: Request targeted schema, docs, migration, credential, or listener-routing changes before exposing the contract publicly.

options.title: Pause for broader design
options.body: Hold or close this branch if maintainers want a cross-channel account model before Teams ships its own account shape.

recommendation.title: Accept the PR contract
recommendation.body: Land the current contract with the existing exact-head checks and live Teams proof as the first supported Teams multi-account shape.
